name: Repos
description:
The Repos API allows users to manage their git repos. Users can use the API to access all
repos that they have manage permissions on.

Databricks Repos is a visual Git client in Databricks. It supports common Git operations
such a cloning a repository, committing and pushing, pulling, branch management, and visual
comparison of diffs when committing.

Within Repos you can develop code in notebooks or other files and follow data science and
engineering code development best practices using Git for version control, collaboration,
and CI/CD.

methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Creates a repo in the workspace and links it to the remote Git repo specified.
Note that repos created programmatically must be linked to a remote Git repo, unlike repos
created in the browser.

required_fields.name: url
required_fields.description: URL of the Git repository to be linked.

required_fields.name: provider
required_fields.description:
Git provider. This field is case-insensitive. The available Git providers are `gitHub`,
`bitbucketCloud`, `gitLab`, `azureDevOpsServices` (Azure DevOps Services, including
Microsoft Entra ID authentication), `gitHubEnterprise`, `bitbucketServer` (Bitbucket
Data Center), `gitLabEnterpriseEdition` (GitLab Self-Managed), and `awsCodeCommit`.

Data Center), `gitLabEnterpriseEdition` (GitLab Self-Managed), and `awsCodeCommit`.

all_fields.name: git_credential_id
all_fields.description:
Git credential ID to use when cloning the repository. The Git credential must be
configured for the current user.

all_fields.name: path
all_fields.description:
Desired path for the repo in the workspace. Almost any path in the workspace can be chosen.
If repo is created in `/Repos`, path must be in the format `/Repos/{folder}/{repo-name}`.

Data Center), `gitLabEnterpriseEdition` (GitLab Self-Managed), and `awsCodeCommit`.

all_fields.name: sparse_checkout
all_fields.description:

methods.name: List
methods.description:
Returns repos that the calling user has Manage permissions on.
Use `next_page_token` to iterate through additional pages.

Deprecated: This operation does not return a complete list of the repos in the workspace, because
repos with the Git CLI enabled are not included in its results. Instead, use the Repos and
Workspace APIs to find repos and their associated metadata in the workspace.

all_fields.name: next_page_token
all_fields.description:
Token used to get the next page of results. If not specified, returns the first page of
results as well as a next page token if there are more results.

all_fields.name: path_prefix
all_fields.description:
Filters repos that have paths starting with the given path prefix.
If not provided or when provided an effectively empty prefix (`/` or `/Workspace`)
Git folders (repos) from `/Workspace/Repos` will be served.

poll_field.name: next_page_token
poll_field.description:
Token used to get the next page of results. If not specified, returns the first page of
results as well as a next page token if there are more results.

methods.name: Update
methods.description:
Updates the repo to a different branch or tag, or updates the repo to the latest commit on
the same branch.

required_fields.name: repo_id
required_fields.description: ID of the Git folder (repo) object in the workspace.

required_in_url_fields.name: repo_id
required_in_url_fields.description: ID of the Git folder (repo) object in the workspace.

all_fields.name: branch
all_fields.description: Branch that the local version of the repo is checked out to.

all_fields.name: dangerously_force_discard_all
all_fields.description:
WARNING: DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. If true, permanently deletes ALL uncommitted
changes in the Git folder — staged, unstaged, and untracked files — before updating.
Lost data CANNOT be recovered.

NEVER use this on Git folders where users author or edit files. This flag is intended
ONLY for automated jobs that treat the Git folder as a read-only mirror of a remote
branch and need to force-sync it. If any user has uncommitted work in the Git folder,
that work will be permanently destroyed without warning.

Local commits that have been made but not yet pushed to the remote are preserved.

all_fields.name: git_credential_id
all_fields.description:
Git credential ID to use for this update operation. The Git credential must be
configured for the current user.

all_fields.name: repo_id
all_fields.description: ID of the Git folder (repo) object in the workspace.

all_fields.name: sparse_checkout
all_fields.description:
If specified, update the sparse checkout settings. The update will fail if sparse checkout is
not enabled for the repo.

all_fields.name: tag
all_fields.description:
Tag that the local version of the repo is checked out to. Updating the repo to a tag puts
the repo in a detached HEAD state. Before committing new changes, you must update the repo to
a branch instead of the detached HEAD.

required_positional_arguments.name: repo_id
required_positional_arguments.description: ID of the Git folder (repo) object in the workspace.
